content.intro: This lesson covers Borrowing and References. It sits in Module 6, Ownership and Borrowing, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Borrowing and References matters when you work with value ownership and reference validity. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A reference borrows a value rather than owning it. The borrow checker checks that references stay valid and that mutable access does not conflict with other active borrows.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Borrowing and References, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Ownership and borrowing are central prerequisites. Resolve the compiler message by clarifying who owns a value and how long each borrow needs to remain valid, rather than adding clones indiscriminately.
